papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

literature_themes.theme: Optimizing Resource Allocation in Cloud and mmWave Networks Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on the development of advanced resource allocation strategies in cloud computing and mmWave integrated access and backhaul (IAB) networks. Both studies leverage Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to enhance performance under dynamic conditions, addressing challenges such as resource underutilization, service delays, and mobility-induced link outages. The proposed algorithms aim to improve efficiency and adaptability in resource management, ensuring better user throughput and cost-effectiveness.
literature_themes.limitations: The studies highlight limitations in existing optimization strategies, such as static resource allocation methods that fail to adapt to rapidly changing workloads and environmental conditions. Additionally, the performance of the proposed algorithms may still be constrained by the complexity of real-world scenarios, including varying user mobility patterns and unpredictable network dynamics.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies a significant research gap in the integration of adaptive algorithms for dynamic environments, particularly in the context of multi-cloud strategies and mmWave networks. By exploring MARL approaches, future research can build on these findings to develop more robust solutions that effectively manage resource allocation in increasingly complex and variable network conditions.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing emphasizes the development of adaptive strategies to optimize resource management in cloud and mmWave networks. Key studies demonstrate that MARL can enhance performance under varying conditions, addressing issues like resource underutilization and service delays. However, limitations in adaptability and practical implementation in real-world scenarios highlight significant research gaps, suggesting a need for further exploration of robust, adaptive algorithms in complex environments.
scholarly_positioning: While existing research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has made strides in optimizing resource allocation in cloud and mmWave networks, significant limitations persist regarding adaptability to dynamic environments and practical implementation. Current approaches often rely on static optimization strategies that fail to respond effectively to fluctuating workloads and user mobility, leading to resource underutilization and service delays. Moreover, theoretical frameworks have not sufficiently addressed the complexities of real-world scenarios, leaving a gap in practical applications of MARL. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing robust, adaptive MARL algorithms that can dynamically manage resource allocation in increasingly complex cloud computing environments, thereby contributing to the broader discourse on efficient resource management in the face of rapid technological advancements.

research_scope: This study will focus on developing and evaluating a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in multi-cloud computing environments, specifically targeting virtual machine allocation under varying workloads and user mobility. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the proposed MARL algorithms will be tested against traditional static allocation methods. The primary outcomes will include resource allocation efficiency, measured by throughput and latency, while secondary outcomes will assess adaptability to changing workloads and user mobility patterns. The study will also incorporate real-world deployment scenarios to address practical implementation challenges and validate the theoretical findings.
concept_definition: 1. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL): A framework where multiple agents learn to make decisions and optimize actions in a shared environment to achieve individual or collective goals. 2. Dynamic Resource Allocation: The process of distributing computing resources (e.g., virtual machines) in real-time based on current demands and conditions. 3. Cloud Computing: A model that enables on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources. 4. Virtual Machine Allocation: The assignment of virtual machines to physical servers based on workload requirements. 5. Workload: The amount of processing that a system must handle at any given time, which can vary significantly. 6. User Mobility: The movement of users across different locations, affecting their resource demands and access patterns. 7. Throughput: The rate at which tasks are completed or data is processed in a system. 8. Latency: The time delay between a request for data and the delivery of that data. 9. Real-World Deployment Scenarios: Practical implementations of the proposed algorithms in actual cloud environments to evaluate performance and challenges. 10. Adaptability: The ability of the MARL algorithms to adjust to changes in workloads and user mobility in real-time.
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible but requires access to open-source MARL frameworks for development and evaluation. It will need GPU resources for training and testing the algorithms effectively. Additionally, real-world deployment scenarios may require access to deployment data from cloud environments. Since the study does not involve human participants or sensitive data, ethics approval is not necessary. To enhance adaptability, it may be beneficial to incorporate real-time data on user mobility and workload fluctuations, which could involve partnerships with cloud service providers for data access.

Assumptions that require empirical validation include the effectiveness of real-time data integration and the extent to which user mobility impacts resource demands.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop and evaluate a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in multi-cloud computing environments, specifically focusing on virtual machine allocation under varying workloads and user mobility. Key concepts include MARL, dynamic resource allocation, cloud computing, and adaptability, defined operationally to ensure clarity in measurement. The study is technically feasible, leveraging open-source MARL frameworks such as Ray RLLib and requiring access to GPU resources and real-world deployment data from cloud service providers. Building on existing literature that highlights limitations in adaptability and practical implementation, this research addresses a significant empirical gap by investigating the effectiveness of adaptive MARL algorithms compared to traditional static methods in real-time scenarios, particularly emphasizing the unique challenges of multi-cloud environments, such as heterogeneous resource availability and inter-cloud communication latencies. The theoretical mechanism posits that adaptive MARL algorithms (independent variable) enhance resource allocation efficiency (dependent variable) through mediating factors of user mobility and workload fluctuations, while the complexity of the cloud environment serves as a moderator. The hypothesis states that adaptive MARL will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency, particularly under dynamic conditions, and is falsifiable through measurable outcomes of throughput and latency metrics. Construct operationalization will measure algorithm performance through simulation logs and system performance data, utilizing metrics such as average throughput (tasks completed per second) and latency (response time in milliseconds). The methodology involves developing a MARL framework within a simulated environment, comparing it against traditional methods over a six-month evaluation period, with appropriate controls established through baseline static allocation methods. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in adaptive MARL, technical innovations in real-time data integration, empirical evidence demonstrating improved efficiency, and practical guidelines for real-world deployment. Key limitations include potential algorithm convergence issues, data sparsity, and the influence of external network conditions, which will be mitigated through robust statistical analysis and partnerships for data access, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the proposed framework's applicability.

candidates.text: Develop a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework that utilizes a simulation environment to model dynamic workloads and user mobility.
